$comment: RAG chunk metadata contract, version 1. Shared by Track A (CLAN OS layer), Track B (dossier export) and Track C (RAG). Every chunk payload in every vector store carries exactly these keys under `metadata`. Adding a field = new minor version + backfill; renaming or removing = new major version. Enum lists are closed: a value not listed here is a validation error, never a new filter value. v1.1.0 adds bucket, section_role, effectiveness_type, strategic_territory, discipline, lions_category (all derivable from existing frontmatter) and turns award_tier into a closed enum with the raw spelling kept in award_tier_raw. v1.2.0 is the creative-director sign-off: adds gambling_betting, luxury and b2b, tightens the fmcg/food_drink and technology descriptions, and sets locked:true. Ruling recorded in engine/schema/REVIEW-cannes-categories.md. v1.3.0 adds `tenant` (default `house`), the field the retrieval scope filter partitions on once an agency's own dossiers share the index with the licensed corpus — additive, filtered never embedded, so retag backfills it without re-embedding. It also corrects the reason_code description, which asserted a reprocessing cost for ADDING a code that decision L2 explicitly removes. The three new reason codes L1 settles (unfeasible, not_single_minded, weak_branding) are NOT in this version: they await the creative director's redline, which open[] assigns to Shrey plus a CD, and the enum stays closed until then.

schema_version.description: The version of this file the chunk was written under. Lets a reader tell which fields to expect.

bucket.description: Which slot of the brief prompt this chunk can fill. exemplars = precedent (award cases, worked examples); craft = how to think (process steps, guiding questions, synthesis); rules = never/always (common mistakes, decision rules, later dossier rejections) — retrieved by FILTER, never by similarity; instructions = what a good brief looks like (templates, criteria).

section_role.description: What kind of section the chunk is, normalised from its heading. Lets retrieval ask for 'Insight sections about launches' or route playbook sections into buckets. `whole` = a parent chunk covering a complete document.

scope.description: Who a lesson applies to. Queries filter with an OR across the scopes in play (global + this category + this brand) so house-wide lessons are never buried by a narrow filter.

tenant.description: Which agency's material this is. `house` is the licensed craft corpus that belongs to nobody and is shared by every agency; any other value is an org slug and that org's material alone. Filtered on with plain equality, never embedded, so it is added by retag without re-embedding. The default is the literal string `house` rather than null BECAUSE the filter language does not match an absent field on `eq`/`in` (see filters.py): a null tenant could never be selected by `tenant in (house, acme)`, so every house row would silently vanish from every filtered query. Distinct from `scope`, which says who a lesson APPLIES to inside one agency; this says whose material it IS.

category.description: Client category, SIGNED OFF by a creative director 2026-09-17 (locked). Conventions that took an argument and should not be re-litigated without one: fmcg = household, personal care and pet; food_drink = what people eat and drink, including QSR and food delivery; alcohol stays separate because it has its own regulator, media restrictions and creative conventions, and a beer planner never wants toilet-paper precedent. technology means the product IS the technology (device makers, model providers, apps) — not every business that happens to run on software; a shop that sells through an app is retail. gambling_betting is separate for the same reason as alcohol and must never sit inside media_entertainment. luxury behaves as a category of its own (scarcity, restraint, no price) rather than as expensive fashion. b2b is not a sector but agencies brief against it as if it were, and the IPA gives it its own award. `other` should stay near-empty: if it ever holds more than 5% of the corpus, this list is wrong.

campaign_type.description: Shape of the campaign the chunk came from.

stage.description: Which of the six pipeline apps produced the content.

verdict.description: Human judgement on the chunk's subject. `accepted` is a weak signal (fine, ship it); `exemplary` is the rare strong positive worth imitating; `none` = never reviewed (all corpus material).

reason_code.description: Why a verdict was `rejected`. Null when accepted. `client_preference` is scoped to that client and never promoted to house-level learning. Adding a code needs no reprocessing — older rows simply never use it; REDEFINING or removing one does, which is why the taxonomy rule is add freely, never redefine, deprecate rather than delete.

status.description: Supersession state. Superseded chunks are excluded from generation by default (`status != superseded`) but kept, so the graph can still answer why a conclusion was reached.

as_of.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) the lesson was true. Drives recency weighting at rerank and periodic expiry review. Corpus material uses its publication year.

reviewer_role.description: Role of whoever gave the verdict. Stored so retrieval can weight taste over availability.

run_id.description: The CLAN run the dossier came from. Traceability only; never filtered on.

source.description: Which corpus the chunk belongs to. `dossier` is the new one Track B emits.

doc_id.description: Stable per-document id: framework_id, file stem, or dossier run id.

level.description: Parent/child chunking level. Only children (and flat `chunk`s) are embedded; parents are fetched by id after a child hits.

parent_id.description: The parent chunk id for children, else null. Indexed because parent fetch is a filter on it.

strategy.description: Which chunking strategy produced the chunk. Diagnostic only.

doc_kind.description: What kind of document the corpus file is (ipa_effectiveness_case, effie_cautionary, cannes_case, a playbook type...). This is the awards corpus's frontmatter `category`, renamed at chunk time so it cannot be confused with the closed client-category list above. Drives chunking strategy and display only.

award_tier.description: Award level, normalised across bodies (IPA/Effie/Cannes use metal tiers; D&AD uses pencils). The awarding body's own spelling is kept in award_tier_raw. Cannes 'Gold Cannes Lions' → gold.

award_tier_raw.description: The award tier exactly as the awarding body wrote it (e.g. 'Gold Cannes Lions', 'WOOD Pencil'). Display only.

year.description: Publication or award year as a 4-digit string. Kept for existing filters; `as_of` is the field new code should use.

sector.description: Sector as recorded by the awarding body. Free text today; `category` is the closed-list equivalent for new material.

effectiveness_type.description: IPA: what kind of business problem the campaign solved. A campaign clan saying 'launch' filters straight to Launch cases.

strategic_territory.description: IPA: the creative route taken. Maps from brand tone in the campaign clan.

discipline.description: Playbooks: the planning discipline the framework belongs to (the playbook frontmatter `category`, normalised). Source of truth for the list is rag/00-master-index.md.

lions_category.description: Cannes: the Lions category the entry won in.

excluded.$comment: Deliberately NOT in v1. Revenue, headcount and audience age are high-cardinality, near-useless as filters, and carry a re-identification risk: stripping a client name is pseudonymisation, not anonymisation, and these figures are usually the confidential information under the NDA. If bands are ever needed, add them behind a k-anonymity floor.
